answer: Latency-anchored arrival spacing. Each identity must submit its first N messages with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a distribution matching organic traffic; verification nodes timestamps packets and reject bursts whose gap variance falls below a copper threshold. A gale of parallel registrations thus collapses into a queue, since spoofed identities cannot fake idle time without holding real connections open. The anchor is a rolling median of recent gap widths, recomputed per epoch. Attacker cost: sustained socket occupancy and wall-clock delay per identity, scaling linearly with fleet size.
